ai.overview: The Calgary Flames put their Belt Holders championship on the line for the first time in this reign when they host the Chicago Blackhawks on November 21, 2026. Calgary claimed the belt with their recent 5–2 victory at San Jose and will look to begin a defensive streak at home. The Blackhawks, who have held the belt 241 times previously, trail 90-93-26 in the all-time series but know exactly what it takes to capture lineal gold.
key_matchups: Calgary's immediate test: The Flames are 10-12 this season and face a Chicago team that just posted 6 goals against Toronto
Chicago's road woes: The Blackhawks are 6-15 overall and suffered blowout losses of 2–9 and 1–4 in their last road stretch
Recent history favors Calgary: The Flames won 3-1 in January and have taken 3 of the last 5 meetings
ai.betting_angles: Calgary enters as the Elo favorite with home ice and a slightly better 10-12 record compared to Chicago's 6-15 mark. Both teams are riding one-game winning streaks, but the Flames showed offensive balance in their 5–2 belt-winning performance while Chicago's defense has been shaky, allowing 5 goals to Winnipeg and 9 at Carolina in recent outings. The head-to-head history is nearly even at 90-93-26, though Calgary has won the last meeting and three of the last five.
ai.prediction_writeup: The Flames should hold serve in their first belt defense, banking on home ice and their Elo advantage against a Blackhawks squad that sits at 6-15. While Chicago showed offensive firepower with 6 goals against Toronto, their recent road results include a 2–9 drubbing at Carolina and a 1–4 loss at Tampa Bay. Calgary has won 3 of the last 5 meetings between these clubs, including a 3-1 decision in January. The Flames' 5–2 performance at San Jose suggests enough offensive rhythm to protect the belt, even if their 10-12 record indicates inconsistency.
